baker: The oven does not care about my feelings, only the flour.
farmer: The soil remembers who was kind to it.
Rain is a loan, not a gift.
smith: Hot metal teaches patience. Or burns.
Bring ore and I will bring edges.
guard: I watch the road so you can complain about the prices.
Wolves keep to the wilds, mostly.
miner: The deep rock hums at night.
Ore does not dig itself, whatever the tavern says.
fisher: The river is honest. The fish are not.
A slow day means a long story.
innkeeper: Everyone sleeps eventually. I count on it.
Twelve coins, a bed and no questions.
herbalist: Half of medicine is knowing which leaf not to chew.
Moss for aches, mint for manners.
merchant: Prices are weather you can argue with.
Buy where it is cheap, sell where it is missed.
default: Keep your coins close and your friends closer.

sunny: Sunny Town is small, but the bread is loud.
They say the old mill still grinds at night.
copperhead: The mountain keeps what it wants. We keep the rest.
Copperhead rings with hammers from dawn.
saltmere: Mind the bridges after rain, they sing.
highmarket: Highmarket never closes, only changes hands.
The ring wall was built to keep prices in.

hungry: My stomach is filing a complaint.
If I smell bread, I am following it.
fed: Good day to be on two legs.
night: The lanterns look kinder after dark.
morning: The town is waking up. So am I.
hero: If a wolf comes in here, I will have words with it.
I do not run from wolves. Mostly.
mayor: A town is just a ledger with chimneys.
Every coin in the treasury has a name on it.
raid: Wolves at the edge! Stay close to the guards.
I heard howling past the wall.
